content.question: Which attribute in a RelativeLayout attaches a view to the left edge of its parent?
content.explanation: The instructor used android:layout_alignParentLeft (and related alignParentTop/Right/Bottom) to attach views to parent edges.
hints: It's an alignParent... attribute.
Used specifically in RelativeLayout for attaching to a side.

content.question: What is the difference between padding and margin as explained in the episode?

options.text: Padding compresses inner space; margin controls outside/alignment spacing.
Padding controls outside spacing; margin compresses inner space.
Padding only affects text size; margin only affects background color.

content.explanation: The instructor stated padding reduces inner space (inside a container) while margin is used for aligning items and outside spacing.
hints: Padding is internal; margin is external.
He demonstrated removing padding to remove gaps.

content.question: What does 'layout blending' refer to in the lesson?

options.text: Combining different layout types (e.g., RelativeLayout inside LinearLayout) to build the UI.
Applying CSS-like blend modes to Android views.
Using only a single layout type for all UI pieces.
Automatically merging resource files at build time.

content.explanation: Layout blending was shown as nesting and combining different layouts (relative inside relative, linear inside relative, etc.) to achieve the design.
hints: He described it like a 'milkshake' of layouts.
It involves nesting different layout types.

content.question: Which root layout did the instructor use when placing the four corner text views?
content.explanation: The instructor said the root container was a RelativeLayout and then used child relative layouts for blending.

RelativeLayout supports alignParent* attributes.

content.question: According to the episode's 'colour theory', what percentage of the screen does the primary colour typically occupy?
content.explanation: The instructor defined primary colour as roughly 90% of the screen, with secondary ~9% and tertiary ~1%.
hints: Primary is the dominant background colour.
Secondary and tertiary are much smaller percentages.

content.question: Which asset type did the instructor recommend for scalable icons in Android Studio?

options.text: Raw bitmap from URLs at runtime

content.explanation: He used Vector Asset (clipart or SVG import) via Asset Studio so icons become XML vector drawables suitable for scaling.
hints: The file produced by Asset Studio was an .xml vector drawable.
Vector assets scale without quality loss.

content.question: Why did the instructor say a downloaded avatar with a white background caused an issue?

options.text: Because the white background of the image hid the layout's background colour, making it look wrong.
Because Android doesn't support PNG images.
Because images cannot be used inside CardView.
Because images must always be fetched from the internet at runtime.

content.explanation: He noted the downloaded avatar had a white background so the intended pastel background couldn't show through; using vector assets or SVG fixes this.
hints: He removed the white background by importing an SVG as a vector drawable.
Transparent backgrounds let the card's colour show.

content.question: Which CardView attribute did the instructor adjust to make rounded corners?
content.explanation: He changed the corner radius (cornerRadius) on the CardView to create smooth, rounded shapes for the avatar container.
hints: He tried values like 35dp to get the rounded effect.
This attribute controls the roundness of the card corners.

content.question: When importing an SVG through Asset Studio, what output file type did the instructor show is created in drawable?

options.text: A direct SVG file (.svg) left in drawable

content.explanation: Asset Studio converts clipart or imported SVGs into XML vector drawable files (person.xml), not PNGs or raw SVG files.
hints: He pointed out person.xml was produced after import.
Vector drawables are XML in the drawable folder.

content.question: Which attribute did the instructor use to center an ImageView inside a LinearLayout?
content.explanation: He used layout_gravity='center' on the ImageView so it centers within the LinearLayout (or the container's available space).
hints: He explicitly set layout gravity to centre for the image size (e.g., 50dp).
layout_gravity affects the view's position inside its parent.
